paragraphs.text: Destroy not, preserve me from this ambush. See Psa 57:1, title.
paragraphs.anchor: Al-taschith

paragraphs.text: But were disappointed by Michal shifting him out of the way, preferring a husband before a father, though she had otherwise no great goodness in her. The glory of this deliverance David wholly ascribeth to God, and seeketh help of him.
paragraphs.anchor: When Saul sent, and they watched the house

paragraphs.text: This psalm is the same in substance with those aforegoing, viz. David’s desire to be delivered from Saul’s craft and cruelty.
paragraphs.anchor: Deliver me from mine enemies, O God

paragraphs.text: Heb. Set me on high, far out of their reach.
paragraphs.anchor: Defend me from them

paragraphs.text: Saul’s assassins and bloodhounds, hired to despatch me.
paragraphs.anchor: Deliver me from the workers of iniquity

paragraphs.text: The seven sons of Saul, say the Rabbis, who were afterwards hanged, 2Sa 21:1-9, with a company of cut-throats attending them (R. Obad. Gaon in loc.).
paragraphs.anchor: The mighty are gathered aqainst me

paragraphs.text: At Saul’s command, never inquiring into the cause, right or wrong; but taking his will for warrant good enough.
paragraphs.anchor: They run and prepare themselves

paragraphs.text: Heb. to meet me, sc. in mercy, Ut occurras et succurras mihi, or, at my calling, as some render it.
paragraphs.anchor: Awake to help me

paragraphs.text: {See Trapp on "Psa 34:15"}
paragraphs.anchor: And behold

paragraphs.text: These pagan Israelites, who might have some heathens also among them, Saul’s slaughtermen, men fleshed in blood.
paragraphs.anchor: Awake to visit all the heathen

paragraphs.text: Heb. that treacherously work iniquity, that do it consulto et data opera, desperadoes, reprobates, destined to eternal destruction.
paragraphs.anchor: Be not merciful to any wicked transgressors

paragraphs.text: sc. To mine house at Gibeah of Saul, hoping to find me then at home again; as if, like the hunted hare, I must needs return to my old form.
paragraphs.anchor: They return at evening

paragraphs.text: When coming the second night also they missed of David they barked and howled like mad dogs, ready to take every one they met by the throat.
paragraphs.anchor: They make a noise like a dog

paragraphs.text: Ferreting and searching after him in all places, and perhaps surrounding the city to surprise him.
paragraphs.anchor: And go round about the city

paragraphs.text: Calling me traitor wherever they come, and seeking to double murder him, viz. by detraction, and by deadly practice. As a fountain casteth out waters, so do graceless men wickedness, Jer 6:7.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, they belch out with their mouth

paragraphs.text: Or, to their lips they add swords; they word it not only, but are armed and well-appointed. But it is well that they blurt out their bloody purposes, and so give warning, Hunc tibi pugionem mittit Senatus; detexit facinus fatuus, et non implevit.
paragraphs.anchor: Swords are in their lips

paragraphs.text: i.e. Who, that we need care for? David’s friends, they thought, durst not utter their discontent; and for God they took no great thought, Psa 10:3; Psa 55:20.
paragraphs.anchor: For who, say they, doth hear?

paragraphs.text: q.d. Thou not only hearest, but jeerest, at their madness, and wilt bring all their purposes to nought with little ado; and, as it were, playing and sporting. See Psa 2:4.
paragraphs.anchor: But thou, O Lord, shalt laugh at them

paragraphs.text: The stronger Saul is the more will I adhere to thee. Or thus, His strength will I reserve to thee; that is, I will turn him over to thee, who act far stronger, to take an order with him; to put a hook into his nose, and a bridle into his jaws, and to bring me at length to the kingdom.
paragraphs.anchor: Because of his strength will I wait on thee

paragraphs.text: Heb. my high place; therefore what need I fear him, or his emissaries.
paragraphs.anchor: For God is my defence

paragraphs.text: Or, God will prevent me with his mercy, sc. before I ask or think; howsoever, in the opportunity of time he will not fail me.
paragraphs.anchor: The God of my mercy shall prevent me

paragraphs.text: See Psa 54:7.
paragraphs.anchor: God shall let me see, &c.

paragraphs.text: Marcet sine adversario virtus, the natural heat decayeth if it have not wherewith to wrestle. Carthage was not to be destroyed, that Rome might not want an adversary. The saints have the relics of corruption left in them for exercise of their graces. "Slay them not," saith David; and the Chaldee addeth, statim, forthwith, or outright, but by degrees rather; "lest my people," my followers and fellow soldiers, forget their skill in arms or thy judgments on the enemies.
paragraphs.anchor: Slay them not, lest my people forget

paragraphs.text: That they may wander, as Cain did, and be restless. Or, shake them to and fro, as meal is shaken in a sieve; let them be dissipated, and by degrees wasted, that they may be as so many standing monuments of the divine justice, ut eo sint illustriora et testatiora tun iudicia, as the dejected people of the Jews are today.
paragraphs.anchor: Scatter them by thy power

paragraphs.text: The Arabians have this proverb, Take heed lest thy tongue cut thy throat. Many a man’s mouth is a purgatory to the master. Hard words must be reckoned for, Jdg 1:15; the Jews find it so, and will do.
paragraphs.anchor: For the sin of their mouth, &c.

paragraphs.text: Cursing men are cursed men.
paragraphs.anchor: And for cursing, &c.

paragraphs.text: But by degrees, as Psa 59:11, slowly, but surely and severely; that they may feel themselves wasted. There may be much poison in little drops, paulatim seu gradatim et in fine penitus corruant (Kimchi).
paragraphs.anchor: Consume them in wrath, &c.

paragraphs.text: Know to their cost; or, let men know.
paragraphs.anchor: And let them know

paragraphs.text: Let these backsliders in heart be filled with their own ways; run about for hunger, as before they did for malice, Psa 59:6. Here the prophet mindeth to mock them, saith an interpreter, Revertantur famelici (Vat.). Sit poena eorum sicur peccatum (Kimchi).
paragraphs.anchor: And at evening let them return, &c.

paragraphs.text: Sicut mendici de ostio ad ostium faciunt, as beggars do from door to door, saith Kimchi.
paragraphs.anchor: Let them wander up and down for meat

paragraphs.text: Murmur against God and men, howling against heaven, as hungry wolves, Isa 8:21. Others understand it thus, Let them run to and fro for meat, that is, to devour me, as Psa 27:2; but surely they shall not be satisfied, but miss their design, though they tarry all night, watching for me.
paragraphs.anchor: And grudge if they be not satisfied

paragraphs.text: That time wherein they thought to have surprised me, 1Sa 19:11, but thou hast secured me. See Isa 65:14.
paragraphs.anchor: In the morning

paragraphs.text: All David’s strength was derivative; in himself he was weak as water.
paragraphs.anchor: O my strength
